utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your examination by Mr. Bakrac will continue in a moment. I remind you that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the very beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness K54.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday it was the end of the day. We spoke about the very beginning of your statement where you said that you spent 14 days at headquarters, and your explanation was that what you meant was barracks. In the first paragraph of your statement, you said that you were in a logistics unit. Did a logistics unit exist at that time at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm saying that in the first paragraph at the end you said: "When I was a driver in the logistics unit." Was there such a thing as the logistics unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that? Logistics? What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. You said logistics unit and you say that you don't know what that means. How did you give this statement? Was the statement first written out in the Serbian language and then translated or can you tell us how it went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave my statement in the Serbian language, but then the interpreter was interpreting. How can I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Then the statement was written out in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was translated for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't translated for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It wasn't translated to you at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you did not even read what it was that you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they read it out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Oh, they read it out to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember all the details that are contained in the statement

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have the statement in front of you? No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we have a hard copy of that statement in B/C/S, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist, I would have hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you look at the very first paragraph of the statement, and you'll see a reference to your training -- go towards the end of the first paragraph. You'll see a reference to: "Our training was fast-tracked and we finished within" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, would you read from there to the end of the paragraph, please. Just read it out to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I was sent to Prizren where I was a driver in the logistics unit." Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you read it out but in actual fact, you don't know what it means at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means -- it's the service for providing services to the army; that is what I heard in the army that that is what logistics was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It was called the logistics unit then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, so the second paragraph when you say that you spent it in headquarters, you were actually in barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, one knows what is barracks; it is a staff, a headquarters. That's what I think. I mean, we called it "stab," headquarters, or "baza," base.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's move on because our time is limited. So on the 10th of June you came to Prizren and the 24th of June -- or rather, after 14 days that you spent in the base or barracks, as you said, you were deployed in a village that is called Damjane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And in the village of Damjane you spent two and a half months; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So on the 10th of June, if you came to Prizren then, two weeks, 14 days in barracks, that's the 24th of June, and two and a half months in Damjane, that is mid-September. Now, tell me when was it that you were telling the truth, when you said this or when you wrote in the statement that -- please don't interrupt me. I'm the one who is putting the questions and then you will answer. On the 3rd of August you went on leave and you did not return and you deserted. So what is true out of those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave my statement. I did not pay attention to exact bits of information. I sort of said around two and a half months and then after that I remembered the dates. I remembered the date when I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, today, I asked you yet again, because after giving the statement you remembered. I asked you yet again whether you were in the village of Damjane two and a half months and you said yes, and the difference is not negligible, you know a month and a two, there's a big difference. It's not a question of days. I wouldn't --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: June, July -- oh, then I made a mistake in my statement. When I made the statement I didn't do my math right at those moments. Perhaps they wrote something and I wasn't paying attention to it. All right. Let it be a month and a half rather than two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is not a marketplace. Let's not bargain. Have you read the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the statement but I didn't really pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has answered this question. He has already explained the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we're just to accept the explanation, are we? Is counsel not entitled to inquire into it and challenge it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Well, I think he has put the same question -- "this is not a marketplace" was a comment. It was not a question, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just look at the answer which drew the comment. "All right, let it be a month and a half." It's not surprising the comment was made. Please carry on, Mr. Bakrac. You know, one of the difficulties we have here is the way in which these statements are prepared and we have great difficulty in working out at times whether it's the fault of the person, possibly inadequately qualified who takes the statement or it's the fault of the witness that we end up with these mistakes. It's an unfortunate intrusion into the job we have to do that we have to think maybe we're being unfair to the witness in blaming him and it should perhaps be the investigator. However, let's carry on, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you have to understand the Defence as well, especially in this situation when what was disclosed to us was practically just before the examination began, and when we did not have any opportunity to investigate the locations and everything else. So this is the only way of seeing what the credibility of the witness is and whether he's telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Are you saying this was only recently disclosed? This is a statement from 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's precisely what I was saying yesterday, Your Honour. In September, that's when it was disclosed to us. I'm saying recently, as compared to the date when the statement was actually taken. It was disclosed to us in September 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was disclosed on 26th August, 2006, the day we first filed the application to add this witness to the witness list, but his transcript was part of the Milosevic transcripts, all of which were disclosed to the Defence as part of the overall disclosure at the very beginning of the case, not the statement but the transcript, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So on the 3rd of August, you went to do your military service and you returned to your unit in October; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You were returned in October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement -- and you said that during your direct

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you once again: Did you have an opportunity to read your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I am the one who made a mistake and you are asking me something that is unnecessary right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I am the one who's here to say what is necessary and what is not and it's for the Court to say --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When was it that they returned you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of October. I was 20 -- I was in military investigative prison for 20 days. 20 days later they returned me to the same unit. I am sorry about these mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yesterday you were asked when you had actually returned to duty. Now, tell us as close as you can the date that you were actually returned to your unit after your period in custody.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 21st of October. I have a document at home as well, but I didn't bring it along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Following the 21st of October, however, did you spend 20 days in custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that you were deployed in Combat Group 2. When you say that you were deployed in Combat Group 2, what period of time are you actually referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The period from the 10th of June, I mean when I came to barracks, the 10th of June, and then I was in barracks 14 days, and then after that the village of Damjane, Rogovo and Damjane that was the same thing but we called it Damjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And how many combat groups were you servicing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was out there in the field, it was only that group, that group, that's the group that I provided services to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you serviced all five combat groups. Yet again, what is true out of the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did not spend my entire military service in this combat group. For a while I was in barracks, for a while I was in the 2nd combat group and then the 3rd combat group, and I had other friends of mine, soldiers who were also involved in these shifts a bit, one of us would be there and then another one and we would take shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Oh, this is the third version we hear. Yesterday in your statement you said that you serviced all three -- all five combat groups, you gave them water and food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to explain this to you now as well. A month and a half or two I spent with this combat group, as I already said; then I got a replacement. There was another shift. I went back to barracks. Let's put it that way, and I was on the run, and then I was returned. I did not go out into the field, but from the headquarters I took water to the combat group every third day and then the third one and then the fourth one and then these relations changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you take water to the 5th combat group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you said --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe, maybe, I cannot remember now. It's been a long time and the army was all over Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it's possible that the 5th one was there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What would you say to me if I were to tell you that there was no such thing as a 5th combat group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that was true. I know there was Lopuski Han, I know -- I can't remember now and then this vineyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't really matter this fifth group, perhaps. Well, at any rate, there were combat groups. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you in order for us to go our separate ways as soon as possible -- and we speak the same language so we have to make things easier for the interpreters. We speak the same language. What we are talking about cannot really be interpreted. So Combat Group 2 where you were at first was in Damjane; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what would you say to me if I were to put it to you that you are not telling the truth, that combat group -- that Combat Group 2 was in the areas of Babaj Boks and Zub and there are documents to prove that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You've never heard of Zub?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zupa?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Zub.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, you you've never heard of that, great. Now I'm going refer you to your statement. When you were mentioning where you took the five corpses, you said that you turned at the village of Zub, taking the road towards Dragas, and now you're telling us that you don't know where Zub is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Zur, Z-u-r. It's a mistake. It's a tiny village of Zur instead of Zub, close to the Vrmice border crossing. This is where you turn towards Dragas and then at a bend you can turn towards the mountain and the border post of Stojanovic. It's Zur, not Zub.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the English version of the statement it is also Zur.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You got me confused for a moment there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your combat group you said there were 190 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 160, 190. I never knew the exact figure, just an approximate one. I never counted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And yet again you are telling an untruth. In your group there were 118 people, if you were in that group in the first place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in any case over 100. I said 190, but I didn't count them. I couldn't possibly. I just approximated. If you understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we're on the topic of the combat groups, you said that they were in the area of Prizren, Orahovac, and Suva Reka. Those were the combat groups from your brigade. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will read out that part to you. You say: "There were five combat groups in the area of Prizren, Orahovac, and Suva Reka." Is that untrue, that part of your statement, this being the third, or rather, the second paragraph? "In the area of Prizren (Suva Reka, Orahovac) there were five combat groups."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore you didn't state that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One of the things you may have to bear in mind, Mr. Bakrac, is that the witness's recollection may have been much better when this statement was given than it is now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's been five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us look at some other discrepancies and let us hope they will be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this statement, and still I cannot recall some of the details mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You will read out to us when and if I ask you to. Can you tell us precisely about the establishment structure of your unit. Yesterday we heard that you cannot tell us exactly what brigade you were part of, but can you tell us what was the establishment structure or composition of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What did it comprise, this logistics battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logistics battalion, if we are looking at the logistics battalion as a unit per se. It had a fire-fighting department, maintenance, drivers, and the mess. Is that good enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must be 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us move on to -- oh, one more question. You say you were deployed in the village of Damjane. Is it correct that the camp of the combat group in the village of Damjane was on a little hill in front of the village of Damjane on the border of a forested area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the soldiers slept in tents and containers in the village of Damjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and you forgot the hangar that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Hangar, tents, and containers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How come in your statement you say, then, that Bozidar Delic ordered that you get rid of all civilians and to expel them and then to move into their houses? You are now telling something different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain. When we came there the first day there is a small school in that little village. We termed it Rogovo, although it wasn't, but that's how we called it. There I spent the initial one and a half months, the period that we had difference of opinion on before. When I was absent from the army they remained there, and when I returned they spent some additional time on that place and then moved on to Damjane. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, you were not in Damjane. You are not telling us the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this whole thing was called Damjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the area of the village of Damjane, the village itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I heard it referred to was Damjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the statement is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How can it be correct and now you're telling us something to the contrary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't check the exact toponyms and the maps. I simply referred to it the way others did. We sort of tend to generalise things, we soldiers, and I didn't bother to look into detail what the name of the village is, whose house it was, whose meadow it was, but it was referred to as Damjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The difficulty we have is that you say when you arrived you stayed in a place that you called Rogovo. You were there for one and a half months. Then you were away from the army, as we know. And you say: "When I returned they spent some additional time on that place and then moved on to Damjane." Now, what do you mean by spending additional time in that place and then moving on to Damjane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They moved for the mere 2 or 3 kilometres towards the border. Everything else was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are these two different -- two separate villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bakrac ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you initially were ordered to remove the civilians, where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The area of Damjane. There was a settlement called Rogovo close by. I can't -- I can't explain precisely. It was the area of Damjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were the villagers removed only from part of the area or from the whole of the area that you call Damjane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From one part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what name do you give to that part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We called it Damjane. We sort of referred to it as Damjane. We used it as a reference point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So where does the name Rogovo come into all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rogovo was close by. One could see it from a hill nearby, and you could see Orahovac as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the point of mentioning Rogovo to us? What happened at Rogovo that you've now introduced that into this evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do I know? Some called it Rogovo, some called it Damjane, so I mentioned both. There were different names in use. I didn't understand it, either. I wasn't interested in the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that may be understandable, but one of the things you've said is that you were initially in one place, which you were calling Rogovo, and then after all your various adventures when you returned, you spent some time there and then moved on to Damjane. Now, I don't understand that at the moment and I would like you to help me to understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I can give my statement again and focus on the facts. I was in the village of Rogovo in a school there. This is where the Combat Group 2 was deployed at first, and I spent there a month and a half or so. When I deserted, when I left the army, I was absent for --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but this is important. The witness said Rogovo, and I don't see it in the transcript, the name of the village where he was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Upon my return, I didn't go out in the field. I merely provided my services to Rogovo. I took water to the troops there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But a part of your statement is about clearing a place, a village, as you describe it, of all civilians, which is the bit of your evidence that really matters, if it's true. And what we're trying to establish is where the hell was that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in Rogovo. That's where we had ordered the civilians to leave their homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please have Exhibit P45 on e-court. It's a map, and perhaps on that map he can indicate to us where Rogovo is and where Damjane is. No, no, please scroll down. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you show us Damjane and Rogovo on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Rogovo" here. It's a tiny place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher's assistance in marking that spot and perhaps we should assign it an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Rogovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please put the number 1 or A there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's the number 1, okay. Could you please put the number 2 next to Damjane.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. And Damjane are close to the border.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may. First we were here. This we called Rogovo. A few months later we moved somewhat to here. It's not much, but I spent a month and a half or even as much as two months here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, for a month and a half or two you were --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is the camp on the hill where the troops slept under tents and in containers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I slept at the school throughout, but this is where the camp and the containers and the hangar was where I am placing a mark now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was the school in the village of Rogovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This map is now meaningless. So if you're going to use this in a productive way, you're going to have to start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot stop the witness. I cannot stop him from marking things on the map. I really am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just explaining this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the map back on e-court to mark it properly because this is really ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now what it is that you want me to explain to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you draw Rogovo for me for one, 1, Rogovo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look at this, a little dot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I find it difficult to know why we need marks for certain things at all on maps. It is clear where Rogovo is said to be on this map. It's equally clear where Damjane is said to be. What we need to know is where is the school. Now, is it inside Rogovo or outside of Rogovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I wanted to say. I wanted him to mark where the school was. Your Honour, Your Honour, I beg your pardon, I wanted Rogovo to be 1, Damjane 2, and the school number 3, and not to have him draw anything else on the map and to tell us where the school is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you go. You've got it all on the map now. I drew it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this school in Damjane or Rogovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Damjane and Rogovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you also just tell us where the camp was before you were in the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've told us about a camp that consisted of tents, containers, and a hangar. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this village of Damjane. That's where the hangar was and the tents and these containers. As for this village where the school is, the school was there and the houses around the school before Damjane, between Rogovo and Damjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we'll need the map any longer. Could it please be assigned an IC number. Now I'm going to move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your statement on page 3, you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You spoke about an action between the 1st and 3rd of August, 1998. And in your statement you said: "On that day Colonel Delic was with a group, too. A tank was at the head and I was right behind the tank. The infantry is -- was towards the end of this group." As far as I understood your testimony and transcript, you were right behind the tank with a water truck. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In terms of establishment, when a unit goes into action, according to rules of combat, does a water truck follow a tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case, it's not according to establishment, but the cooler of the tank broke down, so I had to add water into the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You're saying that only now after seven years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After seven years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Eight years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the only reason why I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that a tank does not have a cooler at all and no water at all, what would you say to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it sure does. I cannot remember. Well, it's not an 84. The other one. It's the other one. It does have water, it sure does.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What's the other one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the type, because I was not in a unit in order to know what tank and -- I know about the Dites [phoen] and the 110 and the Pince [phoen], but I don't really know about tanks, and it's probably the cooler that broke down, and I had to be there in order to add water to the cooler.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A tank stops and only then a water truck would come and re-fill it with water.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the tank, we travelled -- well, it was getting dark. It was 15 kilometres, so it started getting dark and then we were in Djakovica at 12.00. Now, figure it out, and four hours from Djakovica to Prizren, that's really too much and all of that on account of a tank, and I was by the tank all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You were travelling from Djakovica to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel please not interrupt the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because of the tank because of its broken cooler. I had to be by the tank in order to re-fill it with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The tank did not take part in action at all, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did take part in action, but it just happened, the cooler broke down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Too quick, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the cooler broke down after the action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that is how you moved into action and now you said that you went from Djakovica to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the tank did not get off the road. It did not go into the villages out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it did not go into action. It did not take part in this action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did take part in the action, but there was no need for it to go off the road. It did its firing from the road. It has quite a long range, a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What is this range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. From 7 kilometres onwards. How can I say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what was the village that the tank fired a shell at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medvedce was the village as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The village of Medvedce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meca or Medvedce, I cannot remember any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And it targeted a house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a house, twice, three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That was on the 3rd of August, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Between the 1st and 3rd of August. At what time of day was it? What time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between morning and noon, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the transcript at Mr. Milosevic's trial when he asked you about that, you said to him that you remember full well that that house was targeted and that smoke was coming out of the chimney. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Between the 1st and 3rd of August when the temperature in that area is 30 centigrade, is that right, smoke was coming out of the chimney?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Tell me, Colonel Delic, how did he indicate the house? Did he show the house with his hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 150 and 200 metres, perhaps even 300 metres. I cannot say now. Perhaps it was even 400.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And Who was it that he indicated this to with his hand and who did he tell to start firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer on the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this officer on the tank have a helmet or a cap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this one didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So he was in action on the road, he was standing on the turret of the tank but he didn't have a cap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he did have a cap but it wasn't tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You saw that, that it wasn't tied properly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He could hear Delic, what he was saying to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the one at the turret, he targets -- could you just answer, or rather, wait with your answer. We're moving too fast.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not the only person in the tank. There are other people there, too. There's the driver and then there's the shooter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the one from the turret went down and indicated to him where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it's you that has to wait. It's very difficult for witnesses, and an interpreter can probably cope with a question and answer but when you get the answer you've really got to allow a break. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour, to you and to the interpreters, really. I get carried away by the answer and then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want an answer to this, what you said just now? It wasn't a problem for him just to lean down a bit and to talk to the marksman because it's the marksman who really moves the turret.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Oh, so he just bent over a bit instead of leaned towards him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So how did he know, the shooter, what to do and what -- the gunner, what did he -- how did he know what house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he leaned over I couldn't hear properly because I was watching the house that was supposed to be targeted, and I wasn't really paying attention to every little thing he said to him. But, in fact, I was just waiting to see how the firing would to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was that? You could hardly wait to see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You could hardly wait?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not that I could hardly wait, but it's along those lines. Heaven forbid that I could hardly wait for somebody to get killed, but I was sort of waiting to see what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, as for this house, did you indicate it in 2003 to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It wasn't destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, how did you recognise it, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised it just right, although there were some changes. The man had added some walls to it, altered it in a way. There's even a new water-pump out there. So yes, I noticed that. Everything was sort of altered.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So there were additions made to the house; it was altered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You were in this action just one day, and five years later you recognised the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I recognised it, and I recognised a little hill where we had stopped, and even the kilometres, as far as I can remember. Well, we recognised it. We took a picture of it. And even if we were to go now, I could tell you where it is and where things are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move on to a new topic, or, rather, to the year 1999. In your statement on page 5, you said that at 3.00 in the morning on the 28th of February, on Delic's orders, all five combat groups were deployed in Ljubizda Has. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All five combat groups?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's what you stated in 2002 when you said that your memory was the best.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I remember because there were a lot of unknown soldiers there. And of course I said that all five combat groups were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. And in preparation for this examination, you said to my learned friend of the Prosecution that all five combat groups did not participate at all but that part of one group took part only.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what is correct? Were you lying to us a minute ago or are you lying now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not lying, sir. I changed it because I didn't want to look like a liar. I said that all five groups took part and that is why I changed it. Only part of them took part in this; that's why I changed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please explain to me now when it was that your memory was better, five days ago or in 2002.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that part of the combat group was there, present there. Well, I'm remembering again now. It's coming back to me, other things that happened in Kosovo, but I don't want to talk about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We cannot go outside the confines of the direct examination, so please focus on what I am asking you about. If I tell you that, according to all military and combat documents, on the 28th of February, 1999, there was no action whatsoever in Ljubizda Has, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 28th, the day before that. I know that on the 28th I got very sick and that is why I remember that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You got very sick and you went into action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly on the 28th of February, on that day I caught a cold and I ended up in hospital for five days, and that is why I remember that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You were in hospital for five days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And your claim is that it was the 28th of February -- sorry, just hang on for a second. Let it be the 26th of February. You are saying that it was in the second half of February, this action, and that you ended up in hospital. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, as far as I can remember the dates. I remember the 28th of February because we were in action. We had been in action before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was it maybe December 1998, or January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 28th of February. I think, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Great. Yesterday my learned friend Mr. Ackerman asked you about the action in Jeskovo and you said that it was about two weeks after this particular action. You asserted that you had only seen seven killed civilians; you even said that in the additional information you provided. In the main statement it says that you saw seven corpses, seven bodies, and in the addendum you said that you saw seven civilians. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday Mr. Ackerman presented to you and read out to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the transcript, I would like to say, and perhaps my colleague yesterday didn't know what the number was of our exhibit, so it was the OSCE report, 5D112. Your Honours, I have two other reports as well. They are in English, and I can read to the witness very brief excerpts, to the witness. Please tell me, for the Trial Chamber, should I put this on e-court? All three documents have D numbers of our Defence, so could you please tell me whether the Trial Chamber would like to see it on e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the easy way is -- well, do the interpreters have access to e-court? Possibly not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we do. Yes, we do, but we need to have it on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's have it on e-court, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday Mr. Ackerman read this out. It is 5D112. It is paragraph 4, speaking of the security situation. I think it's on page 3. So it is section 4, rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And why do you need to read it again? Do you have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no -- no, Your Honour. I just wanted -- because yesterday it was not in the system. I just wanted to mark that it is that particular exhibit, 5D112, where the Prizren centre of the OSCE was commenting that the KLA was in Jeskovo, and Jeskovo had before that been an abandoned village for a week. So now could we show 5D113 on e-court for the interpreters as well because it is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So now you confirm that you had seen civilians. The KVM report of the 12th of March, 1999 - that is 5D113 - on page 2, says the following: "C/A20A" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just lower the text a bit. Mr. Hoca Zagradska, Jeskovo. Right. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "C/S20A and 20B accompanied Colonel Petrovic and the Milicija into Jeskovo whilst they carried out an investigation into yesterday's VJ operation in the village. Seven KLA bodies were found to the north and on the outskirts of the village. All were dressed in black overalls, KLA uniform, and had apparently died from small-arms fire. In the vicinity of each body was an AK series weapon." And in the last one: "In a house there was a 57-millimetre mortar set up with six primed mortar rounds nearby. In an adjacent storeroom there were more boxed mortar rounds. The mortar was slightly rusty, but it was likely to have been fired recently." So that is 5D113 and it is a report dated the 13th. Another report of the OSCE dated the 13th says: "The teams registered and examined the seven bodies of persons who had been dressed in KLA uniforms, obviously killed during the VJ/MUP operation in Jeskovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. So 5D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you have an impartial OSCE commission that was there in the village of Jeskovo in the action that you referred to. They saw seven bodies and you insist now that they were in civilian clothing. And they submitted a report that these were KLA soldiers with weapons, that mortars were found. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why didn't the army let the OSCE enter right away? But they waited a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You're not the one asking questions here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's my answer. The OSCE wasn't able to see it right away. The bodies may have been put in different clothes in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In different clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in an operation before that, when I mentioned the 28th of February, we forebade --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But this report states that the village had been abandoned for seven days and that it was only the KLA that were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps the KLA were there, but I saw a dead male in civilian clothes, in pants and a shirt. If that's a uniform --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you remember the pants and the shirt and their colour seven years later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His arms were spread out, dead. One of them was next to the river. Half of his body was immersed into the water and the rest was on dry land. I remember that full well. As I said, I remember everything bad that took place there. I don't remember any good.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us move on to another topic now. It concerns the operation on the 24th of March in Trnje. In your statement, first you say that you returned to Prizren on the 20th of March, and two days later with your battalion you were deployed to a village close to Novaci. Do you know what village exactly it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trnje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trnje, I think. Those are tiny hamlets, some comprising two or three houses. Novake, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, on the 20th of March you were deployed to Trnje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 24th of March we left the barracks. We were not deployed anywhere. It is possible that there was a translation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A translation error. Please wait for me to read it out to you. Therefore, this is incorrect: "The 24th of March I returned to Prizren, and two days later I was deployed with my battalion to a village near Novake." That village is close to Orahovac. This is what you stated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I heard Novaci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't understand what did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that this was the village of Novaci or Novake and I wasn't much interested in it. I just heard it was called Novaci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say here clearly that it was close to Orahovac, close to a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a Serb village, close to it. We went through that village and reached the Albanian one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you stayed there for how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five full days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Five days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the fifth day we returned to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you returned to the barracks on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I will explain. On the 20th I returned to the barracks. On the 24th, when the bombing began, we left the barracks. It wasn't on the 20th, as stated here, but on the 24th we left the barracks and went to that village. We went through Novake, or whatever the name was, and we reached Trnje. There are a lot of villages with similar names there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will read it out again. "I returned to Prizren on the 20th of March, and two days later I was deployed with my battalion part of Combat Unit 2 to a village near Novake. There were about 70 of us. The village is close to Orahovac and next to a Serbian village."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you say you stayed there for five days. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, the statement is incorrect when it states that you were in the village of Novaci close to Orahovac which is much further away from the village of Trnje and you were here to testify about that incident. Was this statement read out to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but a lot of time has passed and I can't recall things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have the occasion to see the statement again five days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please wait for me. Five days ago were you given your statement to re-read it and to possibly correct if there was anything to correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you make any corrections, particularly this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't paying much attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Witness K54, let me clarify something with you. What happened on the 24th of March, on the day of the bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 24th of March in the evening or before midnight, we left the barracks. We went towards the village of Trnje. Supposedly we went through the village, as far as I can recall based on what I heard, and it was called Novaci. We went through that Serbian village and reached the Albanian village of Trnje. We spent a full five days there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Between returning to Prizren on the 20th of March and leaving on the 24th of March, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the 20th and the 24th, I was in the barracks. That's when I returned from my trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at your statement and would you turn to -- Mr. Bakrac, is the part relating to Prizren on page 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in the English it is. I have the B/C/S before me and it is the first paragraph on page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The first paragraph on page 6, if you would look at that, please. And you see the paragraph begins: "On 18 March I went to Nis for my military trial ..." Do you see that paragraph? And you're nodding your head, but I take you can see that paragraph, can you? Answer me, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you read to yourself that paragraph and the next paragraph which begins with the words: "On the 24th of March ..." These are not consistent with what you have just told us. They do not indicate that you spent four days in the barracks until the 24th of March, so which is the correct version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will explain it in detail. On the 18th of March, I attended the trial. I returned with a convoy and it took us two days to come back on the 20th. I spent four days in the barracks and did nothing. I was given no tasks. On the 24th, the air-strikes began.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And then you went to the village of Novaci on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the village of Trnje on the 25th early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us move on. Let us move on. No need to go back to that. If you are able to recall it better now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I have a problem with the villages and their names. I never was very familiar with the area so as to be able to remember all the names of all the villages and towns. I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, your recollection was the best in 2002, and as regards the Trnje incident you said: "We entered the village. We split into teams and moved from one house to the next. I was present" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, could we please move into private session, Your Honour, because I am about to mention some names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please tell me this: You explained this in your statement. I'm not really interested in details, but you returned on a truck with a title Hygijena on it and collected the five corpses of those women. Can you tell me, please, from which location you collected these five female corpses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from which place? You mean from which village?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Where did you find them, in which area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we found two women in front of a house, a courtyard of a house. The other one we found behind a house. She attempted to flee but didn't manage. And then the last two we found in the area where they were fleeing with that old man, in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's outside of the village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite outside of the village, but there's a house and then the field starting right behind the house, maybe some 50 metres from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fifty metres away from the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the other ones as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other ones? Well, we found the other ones in a courtyard of a house, attempting to flee. As they were fleeing, they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said when you went to bury these bodies that you were escorted by two military trucks full of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how is it possible, or rather, how long is that distance -- is that road from Trnje to the place where you did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's hard for me to be quite specific. I said roughly 20 to 30 kilometres; that's the approximate distance. Maybe there's just 15. I wasn't sure because I didn't measure it. But not more than 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you actually see any of the five being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you see any of the five being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You saw two women being killed. Did you see who killed them or did you just see them fall down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just saw them fall down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you didn't see who shot at them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said 20 to 30 kilometres, and you said that there were two military trucks full of soldiers following you. In the last line of the last paragraph on page 7, you say that you stole the trucks for the needs of the army "because we were unable to move about in military trucks due to NATO air-strikes. That was the date when NATO bombing began and when it was at its most intense." Which of the two is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the first two days we didn't really pay attention to whether the military trucks could move about or not. The order came later, the order for the military vehicles not to move about. We had to knock down a wall of a house in order to hide the trucks there. We hid military trucks and we had to use the civilian ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent. So the first five days you were on positions, and when you drove that was the seventh day, because on the sixth day you went back and then on the seventh day you took this Hygijena truck.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a second. On the fifth day we came back and then the sixth day we spent the night, having expelled the Albanians from the house, we spent the night there. And then on the sixth day we came to collect the corpses. That wasn't the seventh day, that was the sixth day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said that after five days there was a ban on the use of military trucks and you had to drive for 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no ban. There was no public ban on using military trucks. It's just that in the period thereafter, what happened was that due to our security we were not allowed to ride around in military trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you say here that you stole trucks for the needs of the army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why did you do that when there was a decree stating that civilian trucks could be requisitioned for the army needs? Why did you have to steal them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We simply did it because we didn't ask anybody for permission. We didn't have a key to start the truck. We had to hot-wire it, so that's how I started it. I hot-wired it. I didn't have a key to start a truck. If you think that the army did it in a polite way, with a key, then, you know, the owner would have had to give us the key.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you hot-wired abandoned trucks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, abandoned ones, but I also remember one that was not abandoned. We asked for a key and allegedly this lady couldn't find it and then we broke down the lock and took the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So she wanted to give you the truck but she was unable to find the key.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She most likely tried to hide it because she wasn't pleased about having to give us the truck, but we took it by force anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say that upon your return to Prizren the barracks was hit and you expelled Albanians from a settlement. Was it settlement or a village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: A settlement. Do you know what it's called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petrovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there a garrison health centre there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So from this settlement of Petrovo Selo, where the garrison health centre is you saw refugees going Djakovica and Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that the road from Djakovica doesn't go through that area at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it does from the direction of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you saw from Djakovica refugees going through that village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said from the direction of Suva Reka and from the direction of Djakovica. I repeated that twice yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You just confirmed to me that it's impossible to go through that area coming from Djakovica because the road doesn't pass through that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went on foot. I worked in the army as a driver, so I moved about and I observed the refugees coming from the direction of Djakovica. It's not that I was standing there petrified. No. I moved about for the needs of the army, so I was able to see refugees in different places, including this place. And yesterday I mentioned that I saw them from the direction of Djakovica and from the direction of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you said yesterday that they passed by you, by the place where you had been stationed for two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that, two and a half months, for as long as the bombing lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And now you're telling us that you actually moved about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had to move about. I had to go take my car there. I had to go to this company called Hygijena to get the truck. I was sent there so I had to move about. I had to be on the move. And naturally I used my eyes, I used them, and I observed the refugees moving. I wasn't blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. What about other soldiers from your unit? They were unable to see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, drivers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just drivers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How could they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we had a gate there. We had a gate there with a ramp, and those who manned it were able to see that. The military mess was there and they could see it, whoever was there. And the soldiers would go to do some shopping and they would be able -- they were able to see the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. K54.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. K54, we will now go back to 1998. Is it true that you don't know the name of a single commander of any of the combat groups that you supplied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true that I don't know. It's just that I can't remember. I know that once there was this - I can't remember now -- actually, I can't tell you now, because we're not in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you don't even know the name of your own commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's true that I don't know, but that's because they changed a lot. They worked in shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you don't know the name of a soldier who told you that he heard Delic cleanse the village of terrorists. I'm referring now to the first village as you call it, Rogovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it but I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When your combat group - I'm now referring to the road that you took from Djakovica I guess to Klina - when your combat group captured two Albanians in a cornfield. Do you remember that part of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who told you -- or rather, do you remember who told you what they said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a soldier from an infantry unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You don't know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence today or based on your evidence today, I concluded that during your stay in Kosovo in July of 2002 you went there with an OTP investigator; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: By the way, let me ask you, do you travel to Kosovo because of your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Except for this trip in 2002, you never visited Kosovo from 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were there with an investigator, when you visited on that occasion, did you show the investigator the location where these two Albanians were found, and I guess pursuant to your statement also killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did he make any notes on that occasion, take pictures or make sketches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not concerning the Albanians but concerning the houses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true then that you took him to the house which, according to your statement, General Delic had ordered that it be targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I showed it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did he make any photographs on that occasion, sketches, or tape this on camera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he did take one picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your discussions with the OTP, were you ever shown those photographs afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who identified the location and its name, the location where this house is located, was it you or the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you visit the village of Damjane with the same investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the village of Rogovo with the same investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We passed by. We passed by the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So when I look at your statement of the -- I can't find the date. In any case, from July 2002 and when Damjane is mentioned in the statement, this was inserted by the investigator. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it as follows: I will read out that part of the statement. "On Monday the 8th of July I toured the area of Kosovo which I had previously described in my statement. The purpose of it was to identify the precise locations." On page 2, paragraph 2 of your principal statement it says: "Damjane, the municipality of Djakovica," and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have written that down. In any case, from a distance I tried to show him where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: From a distance you did that concerning the village of Rogovo. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On that occasion was a sketch made or any footage made of the location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went there with the investigator did you also go to the village of Rakovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you show to him on that occasion some houses or other things mentioned in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I did show him some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the village of Jeskovo with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you go with them to the village of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Whilst in the village of Trnje, did you show the investigator the spot where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did he make a sketch, take photographs, or any footage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took some photographs, but I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your contacts with the Prosecutor's office, were such photographs or sketches or video footage ever shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: While you were in the village of Trnje with the investigator, did you indicate the location at which sergeant Kozlina allegedly killed the group of Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: It's a house; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did he take any photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. We dared not go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever shown any such photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When, or rather, did you go to Prizren with the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K54 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you indicate the house of that Albanian who had allegedly been killed in the outskirts of Prizren?
